metadata.name: Business & Organization Add-on
metadata.description: Business layer: Organization JSON-LD completeness (url, sameAs, contactPoint, postal address) + visible contact and trust links (mailto, contact/about/privacy pages). Merges on top of the default core: --rule=./src/assets/business.json

BIZ-01.name: Organization Schema Has url and sameAs
BIZ-01.description: Organization JSON-LD without url and sameAs leaves the entity unanchored: agents cannot link the brand to its official site or verify its presence on LinkedIn/GitHub/Wikipedia. url + sameAs are the minimum for entity resolution in agent answers.

fix.instruction: Add url (official site URL) and sameAs (array of profile URLs) to the Organization JSON-LD on the homepage.

BIZ-02.name: Organization Schema Has Contact Channel
BIZ-02.description: Agents answering "how do I contact this business" read contactPoint.email from Organization JSON-LD. An Organization with no contactPoint is a dead end for agentic customer journeys.

fix.instruction: Add a contactPoint with a valid email to the Organization JSON-LD. Use a company-domain address, not freemail.

BIZ-03.name: Postal Address Is Complete When Present
BIZ-03.description: A half-filled address (city without street, country without locality) is worse than none: agents and search engines drop partial PostalAddress data, and local-pack listings break. If any address exists, all three parts must exist.

fix.instruction: Complete every address in JSON-LD: streetAddress, addressLocality (city), and addressCountry (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. US). Remove the address entirely if the business has no public address.

BIZ-04.name: Visible Contact Email Link Present
BIZ-04.description: A business page with no mailto: link hides its contact channel from both visitors and agents that scrape visible contact options. Contact must be one click away, not buried behind a form.

fix.instruction: Add a clickable email link, typically in the footer or contact section: hello@example.com.

BIZ-05.name: No Freemail Contact Addresses
BIZ-05.description: mailto links to gmail/yahoo/hotmail/outlook and friends undercut brand trust and hurt entity credibility: agents treat company-domain contact info as the identity signal. The freemail list lives in this rule's selector, not the engine.

check.selector: a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@gmail."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@googlemail."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@yahoo."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@hotmail."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@outlook."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@aol."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@icloud."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@protonmail."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@proton."], a[href^="mailto:"][href*="@gmx."]

fix.instruction: Replace freemail contact links with a company-domain address (e.g. hello@example.com) and publish the same domain in Organization JSON-LD contactPoint.

BIZ-06.name: Contact Page Linked
BIZ-06.description: No link to a contact page means visitors and agents cannot reach the business. The link must exist in the site navigation or footer on every page.

fix.instruction: Add a contact link to the footer or main navigation: Contact. Common variants (/contact-us, /get-in-touch) also match.

BIZ-07.name: About Page Linked
BIZ-07.description: Agents and due-diligence visitors look for an About page to establish who runs the business. A site with no /about link reads as anonymous, which suppresses entity trust.

fix.instruction: Add an about link to the footer or navigation: About us. The page should describe the company, team, and history.

BIZ-08.name: Privacy Policy Linked
BIZ-08.description: A linked privacy policy is a baseline trust and compliance signal (GDPR, CCPA). Agents and users both treat its absence as a legitimacy red flag; paid ad crawlers reject such sites.

fix.instruction: Publish a privacy policy at /privacy (or /privacy-policy) and link it from the footer on every page. A hash-only #privacy anchor does not count.
